assessment: Mid-Semester MCQ Bank (Units I & II, Lectures 1-11)
institution: School of Computer Science, UPES Dehradun
instructions: Each question is a MULTIPLE-RESPONSE item: two or more options may be correct. Full marks are awarded only when all correct options (and no incorrect options) are selected.

questions.question: Which of the following were symptoms of the Software Crisis of the 1960s?

options.A: Projects delivered years late
options.B: Cost overruns of 2-10x the estimate
options.C: Requirements misunderstood or ignored
options.D: Software delivered instantly with zero defects

questions.explanation: Lecture 1 lists late delivery, 2-10x cost overruns, misunderstood requirements, production failures and spiralling maintenance as symptoms; instant defect-free delivery is the opposite of the crisis.

questions.question: Which of the following are phases of Winston Royce's Waterfall model?

options.A: Requirements
options.B: System Design
options.C: Maintenance
options.D: Sprint Retrospective

questions.explanation: Waterfall's six phases are Requirements, System Design, Implementation, Testing, Deployment and Maintenance. Sprint Retrospective is an Agile ceremony, not a Waterfall phase.

questions.question: In which situations is the Waterfall model a defensible choice?

options.A: Requirements are fixed, complete and well understood upfront
options.B: Regulatory compliance demands comprehensive documentation
options.C: Hardware-coupled or embedded/aerospace systems
options.D: A fast-moving market where requirements change frequently

questions.explanation: Waterfall suits stable, well-understood, regulated or hardware-coupled domains. Rapidly changing requirements favour Agile.

questions.question: Which principles did the 1968 NATO Software Engineering Conference promote?

options.A: Apply engineering rigour: specification, design, testing, maintenance
options.B: Development must follow repeatable, documented processes
options.C: Progress, quality and cost must be measurable
options.D: Large software is best built by one or two lone heroes

questions.explanation: The conference promoted engineering rigour, repeatable processes, measurement and coordinated teamwork - explicitly rejecting the 'lone hero' model.

questions.question: Which statements describe the Operations team's world in the Dev-vs-Ops conflict?

options.A: Success = stable, available production systems
options.B: Incentivised to change nothing and avoid risk
options.C: Manages servers, networks, databases and monitoring
options.D: Incentivised to move fast and add as many features as possible

questions.explanation: Ops optimises for uptime/stability, resists risky change and runs infrastructure. Moving fast and adding features is the Development team's incentive.

questions.question: Which of the following are the values the Agile Manifesto prioritises (the 'left-hand' side)?

options.A: Individuals and interactions (over processes and tools)
options.B: Working software (over comprehensive documentation)
options.C: Responding to change (over following a plan)
options.D: Contract negotiation (over customer collaboration)

questions.explanation: The four values are individuals & interactions, working software, customer collaboration, and responding to change. 'Contract negotiation' is the lower-valued right-hand side.

questions.question: Which real consequences resulted from the Dev vs Ops divide under Waterfall?

options.A: Slow, manual, risky and infrequent releases
options.B: Environment drift ('works on my machine')
options.C: Blame culture instead of shared ownership
options.D: Mean time to recovery of less than one hour

questions.explanation: The divide produced slow releases, environment drift, blame culture and poor customer impact. Sub-hour recovery is an elite DevOps outcome, not a consequence of the divide.

questions.question: Which gaps did Agile alone fail to close (motivating the rise of DevOps)?

options.A: Dev still threw releases 'over the wall' to Ops
options.B: Operations were not involved until deployment
options.C: Infrastructure remained manual, slow and fragile
options.D: Continuous customer feedback within the development cycle

questions.explanation: Agile fixed the development cycle (including customer feedback) but left the Dev-Ops wall, late Ops involvement and manual infrastructure unsolved.

questions.question: Which statements about iterative and incremental development are correct?

options.A: Iterative = build, evaluate, refine, and repeat to improve what exists
options.B: Incremental = deliver a working portion of the product at a time
options.C: Agile is both iterative and incremental
options.D: Iterative development requires the final product shape to be fully known upfront

questions.explanation: Iteration refines existing work and can proceed even when the final shape is unknown; increments add working functionality; Agile combines both.

questions.question: Which of the following are recognised roles in Scrum?

options.A: Product Owner
options.B: Scrum Master
options.C: Development Team
options.D: Change Control Board

questions.explanation: Scrum defines Product Owner, Scrum Master and the Development Team (plus stakeholders). A Change Control Board belongs to plan-driven/Waterfall governance.

questions.question: Choosing Agile is appropriate when:

options.A: Requirements are expected to evolve or are not yet fully clear
options.B: Time-to-market is a competitive factor in a fast-moving market
options.C: Real users' feedback should shape the product direction
options.D: A fixed-price, fixed-scope contract locks scope before work begins

questions.explanation: Agile fits evolving requirements, fast markets and feedback-driven products. Fixed-price/fixed-scope contracts favour Waterfall.

questions.question: Which items typically belong to an Agile team's Definition of Done for 'working software'?

options.A: Code written and peer-reviewed
options.B: Automated tests written and passing
options.C: Integrated into the main codebase and deployed to a staging environment
options.D: A 200-page Software Requirements Specification signed off before coding

questions.explanation: The DoD covers reviewed code, passing tests, integration, staging deployment, meeting acceptance criteria and being demonstrable. A frozen SRS is a Waterfall artefact.

questions.question: Which characteristics describe a self-organising Agile team?

options.A: The team collectively decides who does what and how
options.B: Decisions are made by whoever is closest to the information
options.C: Members optimise for the shared sprint goal
options.D: A manager assigns every task top-down before anyone understands the problem

questions.explanation: Self-organising teams divide work collectively after understanding the goal and decide close to the information. Top-down task assignment is the command-and-control model.

questions.topic: Customer collaboration mechanisms & cost of change
questions.question: Which statements about customer collaboration and the cost-of-change curve are correct?

options.A: A dedicated Product Owner represents the customer's interests daily
options.B: Sprint reviews/demos give the customer working software every 1-4 weeks
options.C: Short iterations keep changes in the cheap 'requirements/design' zone of the cost curve
options.D: A change found in production is cheaper to fix than one found during requirements

questions.explanation: Collaboration happens via Product Owner, sprint reviews and a living backlog; short iterations keep change cheap. Changes cost far MORE in production (60-100x) than in requirements (1x).

questions.question: Which of the following are the four pillars of the CAMS framework of DevOps?

options.A: Culture
options.B: Automation
options.C: Measurement
options.D: Sharing

questions.explanation: CAMS stands for Culture, Automation, Measurement and Sharing - coined by Damon Edwards and John Willis.

questions.question: Which statements about DevOps are correct?

options.A: It combines software Development and IT Operations to shorten the delivery lifecycle
options.B: It is first and foremost a culture/mindset shift, not just a set of tools
options.C: It gained momentum from the 2009 Velocity talk '10+ deploys per day'
options.D: It replaces Agile, so mature teams practise one or the other but never both

questions.explanation: DevOps unites Dev and Ops, is culture-first, and was popularised by the 2009 Velocity talk. It complements Agile rather than replacing it - mature teams use both.

questions.question: Which metrics are the DORA 'four key metrics' used to assess delivery performance?

options.A: Deployment Frequency
options.B: Lead Time for Changes
options.C: Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR)
options.D: Change Failure Rate

questions.explanation: DORA's four key metrics are Deployment Frequency, Lead Time for Changes, Mean Time to Recovery and Change Failure Rate.

questions.question: Which statements correctly describe a Minimum Viable Product (MVP)?

options.A: It has the smallest possible feature set but must still actually work
options.B: It must be a usable, deployable artifact - not just a slide deck or mockup
options.C: It is a learning strategy to validate the riskiest assumption with least effort
options.D: It is simply a cheap, buggy, low-quality release

questions.explanation: An MVP is minimal in scope, not in engineering discipline - it must work, be deployable, and maximise validated learning. It is not 'low quality'.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid application deployment strategies discussed in the course?

options.A: Blue-Green deployment
options.B: Canary deployment
options.C: Rolling deployment
options.D: Waterfall deployment

questions.explanation: Blue-Green, Canary, Rolling and Big-Bang/Recreate are deployment strategies. 'Waterfall deployment' is not a deployment strategy.

questions.question: Which of the following are Continuous Integration best practices?

options.A: Maintain a single source repository and commit frequently
options.B: Automate the build and make it self-testing
options.C: Keep the build fast and fix a broken build immediately
options.D: Let developers work in long-lived isolated branches for weeks before merging

questions.explanation: CI relies on a single repo, frequent commits, automated self-testing builds, fast feedback and immediately fixing broken builds. Long-lived isolated branches cause 'Integration Hell'.

questions.question: Which statements about Continuous Delivery vs Continuous Deployment are correct?

options.A: Continuous Delivery keeps a manual human approval gate before production
options.B: Continuous Deployment releases automatically with no human gate
options.C: Both require Continuous Integration as their foundation
options.D: Continuous Deployment needs weaker automated test coverage than Delivery

questions.explanation: Delivery stops at a manual gate; Deployment removes it; both need CI underneath. Deployment requires STRONGER automated test coverage, not weaker.

questions.question: Which statements accurately describe a blameless DevOps culture?

options.A: The first instinct after a failure is to fix the system, not punish the person
options.B: Mistakes are treated as data, not character flaws
options.C: Dev and Ops share on-call and incident response
options.D: It is consequence-free and ignores repeated negligence

questions.explanation: Blameless culture fixes systems, treats mistakes as data and shares responsibility. 'Blameless' is NOT consequence-free - people remain accountable for learning and following process.

questions.question: Which statements about the TDD Red-Green-Refactor cycle are correct?

options.A: Red: write a failing test for behaviour that does not yet exist
options.B: Green: write the simplest code that makes the test pass
options.C: Refactor: clean up the code while keeping all tests passing
options.D: TDD means writing all tests upfront, then all the code in one big phase

questions.explanation: TDD is a tight micro-cycle: Red (failing test), Green (minimal code to pass), Refactor (improve while green) - not a big upfront test-writing phase.

questions.question: Which of the following are 'vanity metrics' that DevOps teams should avoid relying on?

options.A: Lines of code written
options.B: Number of tickets closed
options.C: Hours worked
options.D: Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR)

questions.explanation: Lines of code, tickets closed, hours worked and raw server count are vanity metrics. MTTR is a meaningful outcome metric (one of DORA's four).

questions.question: Which statements about Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and immutable infrastructure are correct?

options.A: IaC is declarative - you describe the desired state and the tool achieves it
options.B: IaC is idempotent - re-running the same configuration yields the same result
options.C: Immutable infrastructure replaces servers with new pre-built images instead of patching them in place
options.D: Immutable infrastructure encourages SSH-ing into running servers to apply manual fixes

questions.explanation: IaC is declarative, idempotent and version-controlled; immutable infra replaces instances with rebuilt images (e.g. containers). You never SSH in to patch an immutable server - you rebuild and redeploy.
